new_statements.quote: The fem. marker is an unstressed –a which is attached to sing. nouns only [...] detáka-m/pur-om nāxoš-e “my daughter/son is sick”. [...] The ending for the direct case, when definite, is unstressed –i for masc. sing. new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File check: (text of EIr II/8 pp. 848-849, iranicaonline, doi 10.1163/2330-4804_EIRO_COM_6022) is present and readable. Every segment of the reported quote is there verbatim at the stated places: 3rd paragraph (nominal system) 'The fem. marker is an unstressed –a which is attached to sing. nouns only', 'detáka-m/pur-om nāxoš-e “my daughter/son is sick”', 'The ending for the direct case, when definite, is unstressed –i for masc. sing.', 'Hasán-i azīat maka “don’t bother Ḥasan”'; closing vocabulary paragraph 'the (north)west-Iranian or “Median” character of the dialect is clearly evidenced by words such as pur “son”, zenía “woman”, zāmā “son-in-law”, kúa “cat”, esbá “dog”,... bāˊla “spade”, x…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is on the final syllable of the (masculine/unmarked) noun (esbá, kiá, Hasán), as in Persian; the singular feminine marker -a is unstressed, so feminine nouns surface with penultimate stress (kúa, kárga, kāláka), and the definite direct-case endings (-i m., -o f.) are likewise unstressed. Tafazzoli's DMBI entry (saved:), drawing on Kiā 1335 pp. 146, 186 and this EIr article, words it explicitly: «اسمهای مفرد مؤنث به مصوّت a (فتحه) بدون تکیه ختم می‌شوند و تکیه بر روی هجای ماقبل آن است؛ درحالی‌که در کلمات مذکر، مختوم به a، تکیه روی آخرین هجا ست؛ مثال: úa = آب (مؤنث)؛ várfa = برف (مؤنث)؛ kiyá = خانه (مذکر)» = 'Singular feminine nouns end in the vowel a without stress and the stress is on the syllable before it, whereas in masculine words ending in a the stress is on the last syllable: úa water (f.), várfa snow (f.), kiyá house (m.).' The general final-stress default is inferred from the accent-marked forms, the 'unstressed suffix' wording and Yarshater's remark that the sound system does not differ noticeably from Persian; no source seen states a rule for verbs.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in any source read.
new_statements.exceptions: Feminine singular marker -a unstressed (penultimate stress on feminine nouns); definite direct-case endings -i (m.) / -o (f.) unstressed (Yarshater). For the sister dialect Āmoraʾi, Lecoq 1989 adds: feminine -a unaccented, plural -gál stressed, oblique -e unstressed. Verb-form stress (prefixes ba-/be-, e(t)-) not described.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, citation forms of nouns and short elicited sentences from Yarshater's 1969 informants (Āštīān town, Māzerī quarter, and Šūra village). No phrase-level or verbal-stress information.
new_statements.identity_note: Yarshater 1987 describes Āštīāni proper (town of Āštīān, Māzerī quarter, and Šūra village; 1969 fieldwork, elderly speakers). Glottolog's asht1244 node also carries the two Tafresh village dialects Āmoraʾi (Saʾeb 1976; Lecoq 1989 EIr) and Kahaki (Shariʿati 1998; Kalbāsi & Shariʿati 2012), which the sources treat as closely related but distinct (Āmoraʾi keeps ö/ü and gender in verbs; Kahaki has to- imperfective and -iya plural). Note the Glottolog coordinate given in the target record (37.75 N, 48.68 E, Ardabil area) does not match Āštīān/Tafresh in Markazi province (~34.5 N, 50.0 E). Vafsi (vafs1240) is a separate node.

sources.locator: EIr II/8 pp. 848-849: paragraph on the nominal system (3rd paragraph) and the closing vocabulary paragraph
sources.note: No headed stress paragraph, but states the feminine marker is 'an unstressed -a' and the definite direct-case ending is 'unstressed -i'; accent-marked citation forms show final stress on masculines (esbá 'dog', kiá 'house', Hasán) and penultimate stress on feminine -a nouns (kúa, xúa, úa, kárga, esbéza, kāláka, zenía, detáka); also says the sound system 'did not differ noticeably from Persian'.
Paraphrases Tafazzoli: feminine -a nouns have penultimate stress, masculine -a words final stress; cites the DMBI article. Tertiary; used only as a pointer.

sources.citation: Tafazzoli, Ahmad. "آشتیانی، لهجه" [Āshtiyāni, dialect]. Dāʾerat al-Maʿāref-e Bozorg-e Eslāmi (Great Islamic Encyclopaedia), vol. 1, article no. 227. Tehran: Markaz-e Dāʾerat al-Maʿāref-e Bozorg-e Eslāmi (text from lib.eshia.ir mirror and official cgie.org.ir web edition 'آشتیان، گویش', which adds in-text refs to Kiā 1335 pp. 146, 186 and EIr II/848-849).
sources.note: Explicit: singular feminine nouns end in unstressed -a with stress on the preceding syllable, whereas masculine words ending in -a carry stress on the last syllable (úa 'water' f., várfa 'snow' f., kiyá 'house' m.). Encyclopaedia entry compiled from Kiā 1335, Moqaddam 1328 and Yarshater's EIr article (second-hand).
